texts.li: [first] {X_nameDef}, a factor of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with the Waystone Book, where the league writes down who deals fairly on the roads and who does not. The colony's page is written in red: the colony {TALE}, and {ENEMY} were the ones wronged. {X_nameDef} says {COUNT} silver, carried to them by the league, would pay them back. The colony can also send someone to dispute the entry, or refuse it, and every league will deal with the colony according to what the book says.

[first,age1] {X_nameDef}, a factor of {FACTION} in a dusty coat, has stopped at the gate and opened the Waystone Book on {X_possessive} knee. The league writes fair dealers in it in black ink and robbers in red, and the colony's page is in red: it {TALE}, and {ENEMY} were the ones wronged. {COUNT} silver would pay them back.

[first,age2] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has left a truck at the road and walked up to the gate with the league's ledger under {X_possessive} arm. The colony's page is in red ink, which the league uses for those who wrong traders: it {TALE}, against {ENEMY}. {COUNT} silver, carried to them by the league, would settle it. If the colony thinks the entry is wrong, {A_nameDef} could dispute it instead.

[first,age3] {X_nameDef}, a factor of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with the Waystone Book on a slate, every entry kept in black or red. The colony's page is in red: it {TALE}, and {ENEMY} were the ones wronged. {COUNT} silver, carried to them by the league, would settle it, or {A_nameDef} could dispute the entry instead.

[first,war] {X_nameDef}, a factor of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with the Waystone Book. The colony {TALE}. {ENEMY} are the colony's enemies now, but the league still writes any wrong done to traders on the road in red. {COUNT} silver would pay them back.

[again] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is back at the gate with the Waystone Book, open at the same page in red: the colony {TALE}, against {ENEMY}, and has not paid. {COUNT} silver would still settle it, and until the colony pays, every league gives it worse terms.

[twice] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come back with the Waystone Book, where the colony's wrong is written twice now: it {TALE}, against {ENEMY}. {COUNT} silver settles it, {X_pronoun} says, and nothing less.

li.label: Pay {ENEMY} back ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: Someone is carrying the silver out to {X_nameDef}, who clears the colony's page in the book and will take the silver to {ENEMY}.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} to argue the entry
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} disputed the entry at the gate, and {X_nameDef} agreed to strike it out.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} disputed the entry, and {X_nameDef} took offence and wrote it in a second time. The colony now owes double.

li.label: Refuse the entry
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} closes the book and leaves. The league will give the colony worse terms until it pays.

lines.li: [paid] Good ink, then, and the road is open.
[struck] Struck out, and may I never have to write it again.
[twice] Twice in red, and the next page is worse.
[red] The book remembers, even when I forget.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a waymaster of {FACTION}, has walked up to the gate with a surveyor's chain over {X_possessive} shoulder. The league is laying {TALE} through the region and would like to lay its stretch across the colony's land. A road gang would camp at the edge of the land for some days and lay a stretch of {BEAST} each day, on a line that runs past the gate. {X_nameDef} asks for the colony's permission.

[fields] {X_nameDef}, a waymaster of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with the route of {TALE} drawn on a map. It crosses the colony's land and runs over {COUNT} cells of its fields, unless the road goes round them. {X_nameDef} asks whether the road gang may lay it straight through.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a staff that has a notch for every day's stretch of road. The league is making {TALE} of packed earth, rammed down by hand, and its route runs across the colony's land. {X_nameDef} asks for the colony's permission to lay it there.

[age1] {X_nameDef}, a waymaster of {FACTION}, has come up the road with the road gang's stone carts behind {X_objective}. They are laying {TALE} in flagstones cut from the local stone, and its route runs across the colony's land. {X_nameDef} asks for the colony's permission.

[age2] A truck from {FACTION}'s road gang has stopped near the gate, and {X_nameDef}, the waymaster, has walked over with the plans. {TALE} is being laid in concrete, a stretch a day, and its route crosses the colony's land. {X_nameDef} asks for the colony's permission.

[age3] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with the route of {TALE} shown on a data slate. It is to be paved tile, laid a stretch a day, across the colony's land and past its gate. The league asks for the colony's permission before it lays any of it.

[their:grateful] The league counts the colony as a fair dealer, so {X_nameDef} has come to ask its permission first. {TALE} would run across the colony's land, laid a stretch of {BEAST} a day by a road gang camped at the edge.

li.label: Lay it across our land, fields and all
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back for the gang; the road will cross the colony's land the straightest way, over its fields where the line runs.

li.label: Lay it across our land, round the fields
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back for the gang; the road will cross the colony's land and go round its fields.

li.label: Not across our land
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} rolls up the map without comment, and the road gang will lay the road round the colony's land.

lines.li: [leave] A stretch a day, and you'll watch it grow.
[leave] The nine waymasters at Harrow Ford would have liked a road like this.
[round] Round it is, and the long way.

IncidentDef.label: nobody on a sickbed is anyone's enemy

texts.li: [litters] Hospitallers of {FACTION} have come up to the gate carrying litters, led by {X_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} that the fight is over and {COUNT} of the raiders still lie where they fell. The order would carry them to its sickhouse, since it holds that nobody on a sickbed is anyone's enemy.

[cart,age2] A stretcher cart of {FACTION}'s order has stopped at the gate, and {X_nameDef} has climbed down with the bearers. {COUNT} of the raiders lie downed on the colony's land; the order would carry them away to its sickhouse, if the colony lets them go.

[one] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a litter and a bearer. One of the raiders is still lying out there, and {X_nameDef} asks to carry this fighter of {ENEMY} to the order's sickhouse. The order holds that nobody on a sickbed is anyone's enemy.

[many] Hospitallers of {FACTION} are at the gate with litters, led by {X_nameDef}. {COUNT} raiders of {ENEMY} and others are lying downed out there. The order would carry every one of them to its sickhouse and ask nothing for it.

[age0|age1] {X_nameDef}, a hospitaller of {FACTION}, has come over the field with two bearers carrying poles and blankets. {X_nameDef} says the order's sickhouses take in anyone, as their founder Aldith did, and {COUNT} of the raiders are still lying out there.

li.label: Let them carry them all away
li.outcome: The hospitallers are going out with their litters, and will carry every one of the fallen raiders off the colony's land.

li.label: Only the worst hurt
li.outcome: The hospitallers carry off the worst hurt of the raiders; the rest are the colony's to deal with.

li.label: They are the colony's to keep
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} says nothing, writes it down in the order's book, and leads the bearers away.

lines.li: [carry] Lift together, gently, and mind the head.
[carry] Nobody on a sickbed is anyone's enemy.
[kept] It is written, and that is all.
[gone] The lamp is lit for them now.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with one of the order's satchels. {TALE} is spreading in the colony: {A_nameDef} has it, and {COUNT} people in all. {X_nameDef} asks to set up a sick room in {PLACE} for three days, with the sick kept together there, the healthy kept out, and {X_objective} giving them medicine on regular rounds.

[herbs,age0|age1] {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has come in with a bundle of herbs and boiled linen. The order heard about the {TALE} in the colony. If the colony lets {X_objective} use {PLACE} as a sick room for three days, the sickness will spread less easily.

[masks,age2] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate wearing a mask and carrying one of the order's cases. {TALE} is going round the colony and {COUNT} people are down with it. {X_nameDef} offers to run a sick room in {PLACE} for three days, using the colony's own medicine.

[nodoctor] {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has heard that the colony has {TALE} and nobody well enough to nurse the sick. {X_nameDef} asks to use {PLACE} as a sick room for three days, doing rounds there and keeping the healthy out.

[age0|age1] {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has walked in over the fields with a lamp hung from {X_possessive} staff, the sign of the order. {X_nameDef} says that wherever {TALE} goes, the order sets up a sick room, and asks for {PLACE} for three days, with {X_objective} giving the sick their medicine on rounds.

[their:grateful] The order remembers the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} came as soon as the order heard about the {TALE}. {X_nameDef} offers to run a sick room in {PLACE} for three days, if the colony agrees.

li.label: Give {X_objective} {PLACE} as a sick room
li.outcome: The sick are going to {PLACE}, and {X_nameDef} is setting out the order's things for the first round.

li.label: Give {X_objective} {PLACE}, {B_nameDef} on the rounds too
li.outcome: The sick are going to {PLACE}, and {B_nameDef} will walk the rounds with {X_nameDef} and learn the order's ways.

li.label: Thank {X_objective}; the colony will manage
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} leaves a little of the order's herbs at the gate and walks back the way {X_pronoun} came.

lines.li: [room] The well stay out, and the sick stay in, and we'll see.
[round] Drink this, all of it, and then sleep.
[caught] It has caught me too, and now I am the one in bed.
[goes] It has a harder road now, and I have a long one.
[thanks] Keep them warm and keep them apart.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. Because of {TALE} in the region, the order would like to set up a field sickhouse next to the colony: a long hut of beds with a lamp lit at its door all night, where the region's sick and wounded would be brought. The sisters would ask the colony for medicine, food and clean cloth, and perhaps for its doctor.

[plague] {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has walked up to the gate wearing a mask. {X_nameDef} says {TALE} is hitting the region hard, and the order needs a place for a sickhouse that the sick can reach. The colony's land would suit.

[war] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate after {TALE}, carrying the order's lamp, unlit, on a pole. {X_nameDef} says the region's wounded have nowhere to lie, and the order would like to put up a long hut of beds next to the colony and light the lamp at its door.

[oursick] {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a cart of bedding. Because of {TALE} in the region, the order would like to set up a sickhouse next to the colony, and the colony's own sick could be treated there too.

[age0|age1] Sisters of {FACTION} have come up the road with poles and bedrolls, and {X_nameDef} is carrying the lamp of Aldith, the order's founder. After {TALE}, they would like to put up a long hut next to the colony for the region's sick, with the lamp hung at its door as a sign that anyone may come.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has come to the gate from a truck loaded with canvas, folding beds and crates of dressings. After {TALE}, the order would like to put up a long hut of beds next to the colony for the region's sick and wounded, with a lamp lit at its door all night.

[their:grateful] The order remembers the colony kindly, so {X_nameDef} has come to ask the colony first. The order would like to set up a field sickhouse next to the colony while {TALE} lasts, with a lamp lit at its door all night.

li.label: Let them pitch it by the colony
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back for the sisters, and the order will raise its sickhouse by the colony.

li.label: Let them, and take our sick in too
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back for the sisters. The order will put up its sickhouse next to the colony, and the colony's own sick will be treated in it.

li.label: Not by our gate
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods and leaves to find another place for the sickhouse.

lines.li: [pitch] The lamp goes up tonight, and stays lit.
[thanks] Somewhere else, then, and soon.
[home] Home now, and gently.
[bell] One ring for the one who goes home.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a drover of {FACTION}, has walked up to the gate ahead of the herd. {X_nameDef} asks for the colony's permission to bring a drove of {COUNT} head of {TALE} across its land. They would graze on the way for two or three days and camp at the far edge.

[fields] {X_nameDef}, a drover of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a long stick and a dog. {X_nameDef} would like to bring {COUNT} head of {TALE} across the colony's land, grazing as they go. The colony's unfenced fields are close to their route, so {X_nameDef} asks for permission first.

[ride] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has ridden up to the gate, with the drove raising dust behind. {X_nameDef} asks for the colony's permission to take {COUNT} head of {TALE} across its land over two or three days, grazing on the way and camping at the far edge.

[age0] {X_nameDef}, a drover of {FACTION}, has walked barefoot to the gate while the drove waits at the edge of the land. {X_nameDef} asks to graze {COUNT} head of {TALE} across the colony's land for two or three days.

[age1] {X_nameDef}, a drover of {FACTION}, has ridden to the gate on a pony with a crook across the saddle while the drove waits at the edge of the land. {X_nameDef} asks to graze {COUNT} head of {TALE} across the colony's land for two or three days.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, a drover of {FACTION} in a wide hat and a dusty coat, has walked up to the gate from the drove's supply wagon. {X_nameDef} asks to take {COUNT} head of {TALE} across the colony's land over two or three days, grazing on the way and camping at the far edge.

[their:grateful] The herding folk remember the colony kindly, so {X_nameDef} has come to ask it first. They would like to take {COUNT} head of {TALE} across its land over two or three days, grazing as they go.

li.label: Let them cross
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back for the drove; it will cross the colony's land and graze its way to the far edge.

li.label: Let them cross, for a toll ({BEAST} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counts out the toll at the gate without a word and goes back for the drove.

li.label: Turn them away
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} turns back to the drove, and the drovers will take it round the colony's land.

lines.li: [cross] Count them with us at dusk, if you like.
[round] Round it is, and the grass is thinner there.
[ride] Ride at the edge with me, and keep them moving.
[on] Up and on, every head of you.

IncidentDef.label: the thief on the drove road

titles.li: The thief on the drove road

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a warden of {FACTION}'s herders, has come to the gate at first light with riders behind. {ENEMY} drove off {TALE} of the colony's yesterday, and the herders found the trail at dawn. They would follow it to the thieves' camp. The colony could send {A_nameDef} with them or let them go alone, and they would bring back what they can.

[ride] Herders of {FACTION} have ridden up to the gate in the morning, led by {X_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} says the thieves who took {TALE} from the colony left an easy trail to follow. {A_nameDef} could ride with them to the thieves' camp, or they could ride alone.

[many] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with riders. {ENEMY} drove off {COUNT} of the colony's animals ({TALE}), and the herders take the loss of a friend's animals as seriously as their own. They are on the trail now and would like {A_nameDef} to come with them.

[!ride,age0|age1] Herders of {FACTION} have walked in at first light following the thieves' trail, {X_nameDef} with a spear and a coil of rope. {ENEMY} drove off {TALE} of the colony's, and the herders mean to follow them. {A_nameDef} could go with them, or they will go alone.

[!ride,age2] Herders of {FACTION} in long coats have walked in at first light following the thieves' trail, {X_nameDef} with a coil of rope over one shoulder. {ENEMY} drove off {TALE} of the colony's, and the herders mean to follow them. {A_nameDef} could go with them, or they will go alone.

[ride,age0|age1] {X_nameDef}, a warden of {FACTION}'s herders, is at the gate with riders and a tracking dog. {ENEMY} took {TALE} of the colony's, and the herders want to get them back. {A_nameDef} could come along, or they will go by themselves.

[ride,age2] {X_nameDef}, a warden of {FACTION}'s herders, is at the gate at first light with riders in long coats and a tracking dog on a lead. {ENEMY} took {TALE} of the colony's, and the herders mean to get them back. {A_nameDef} could come along, or they will go by themselves.

li.label: {A_nameDef} rides with them
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is going out with the herders' riders on the thieves' trail.

li.label: Let them ride alone
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and the riders are off on the trail, and will bring back what they can.

li.label: Let the beasts go
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shakes {X_possessive} head over the lost beasts, and the riders go home.

lines.li: [together] Keep up, and keep low when we come close.
[alone] We count every head at dusk, and yours too.
[thanks] Lost beasts are lost, and the grass grows anyway.
[back] Here they are, and one stays with us for the trail.
[charge] Now, all together, and take the beasts first.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an elder of {FACTION}'s herders, has come to the gate. It is calving time and the colony's land is sheltered, so the herders would like to bring {COUNT} pregnant animals and camp there for some days, until the calves are on their feet.

[age0] {X_nameDef}, an old herder of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. {COUNT} of the herd are close to giving birth, and the colony's land is out of the wind. {X_nameDef} asks to camp there until they have calved.
[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate now that it is spring. {X_nameDef} asks to bring {COUNT} pregnant animals to the colony's sheltered land for some days while they give birth.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef}, an elder of {FACTION}'s herders, has come to the gate with a ledger of the herd. {COUNT} beasts are due to calve this month, and {X_pronoun} asks to bring them to the colony's sheltered ground for it.

[their:grateful] The herding folk remember the colony kindly, so {X_nameDef} has come to the colony first this spring. The herders would like to keep {COUNT} pregnant animals on its sheltered land for some days while they give birth.

li.label: Let them calve here
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is going back for the herd, and the herders will camp on the colony's sheltered ground for the calving.

li.label: Let them, for a toll ({BEAST} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counts out the toll at the gate without a word and goes back for the herd.

li.label: Not this spring
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back to the herd to find other ground before the calves come.

lines.li: [calve] More to count at dusk, soon enough.
[thanks] They'll calve where they stand, then, and we'll manage.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has hurried up from the calving camp. One of their {TALE} is having a difficult birth, and {X_nameDef} asks for {A_nameDef}, the colony's best hand with animals, before it is too late.
[second] {X_nameDef} from the calving camp is at the gate. A {TALE} is having a difficult birth, and {X_nameDef} asks for {A_nameDef}'s help. {B_nameDef} could come too and learn from it.

[age0|age1] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}'s herders has come to the gate with bloody hands. A {TALE} has been in labour since dawn, and the herders have done all they can. {X_nameDef} asks whether {A_nameDef} would come and help.
[age2] {X_nameDef} has come up from the calving camp with a lamp and a coil of rope. A {TALE}'s calf is lying the wrong way round, and {X_nameDef} asks for {A_nameDef}'s help to deliver it.
[their:grateful] {X_nameDef} from the calving camp has come to the gate. A {TALE} is having a difficult birth, and the herders trust {A_nameDef} with it more than they trust themselves.

li.label: {A_nameDef} goes
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is going down to the calving camp with {X_nameDef}.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} is going down to the calving camp with {X_nameDef}, but the calf is lying the wrong way and the birth is going badly.

li.label: {A_nameDef} goes, {B_nameDef} beside {A_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are going down to the calving camp with {X_nameDef}.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are going down to the calving camp with {X_nameDef}, but the calf is lying the wrong way and the birth is going badly.

li.label: The herders know their beasts
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back down to the camp to see it through with the herders.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} goes back down to the camp to see it through with the herders, but the calf is lying the wrong way and the birth is going badly.

lines.li: [come] Quick now, and warm your hands first.
[manage] We've done this since before the drove roads.

titles.li: A shrine on the colony's land

texts.li: Two pilgrims of {FACTION} have come to the gate, {X_nameDef} carrying a staff hung with shells. They believe the {TALE} on the colony's land is a holy place, and would like to set stones and a lamp beside it and bless it. It would take three days, and the colony would have an old shrine that passing pilgrims will stop at.

[ancient] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has stopped at the gate with another pilgrim. {X_nameDef} says the {TALE} on the colony's land is older than any of the peoples here, and holy because of it. They would like to set stones and a lamp beside it and bless it.

[grave] Pilgrims of {FACTION} have come to the gate from the {TALE} on the colony's land, which is older than the colony. {X_nameDef} says nobody ever blessed it, and asks permission to set stones and a lamp beside it and bless it.

[tree] {X_nameDef} and another pilgrim of {FACTION} have come in from the great old {TALE} on the colony's land. {X_nameDef} says many people must have prayed under a tree that old, and they would like to set stones and a lamp under it and bless it.

[landmark] Two pilgrims of {FACTION} have come to the gate from the far side of the colony's land. {TALE} is holy to the fellowship, {X_nameDef} says, and they would set stones and a lamp where it can be seen, and bless it.

[age0|age1] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, nearly blind and led by a younger pilgrim, has stopped at the gate. {X_nameDef} says Old Brannoc, who founded the fellowship, blessed every door he came to, and there is a holy place on the colony's land that nobody has marked. In three days they could set stones and a lamp there.

[age2|age3] {X_nameDef} and another pilgrim of {FACTION} have come to the gate with packs, walking poles and a lamp wrapped in cloth. They believe the {TALE} on the colony's land is a holy place that nobody has marked, and would like to set stones and the lamp beside it and bless it. It would take three days.
[second] Two pilgrims of {FACTION} have found the {TALE} on the colony's land and would like to set stones and a lamp beside it. It would take three days, or two if {B_nameDef} helped them.

li.label: Let them raise it
li.outcome: The pilgrims are walking out to the {TALE} with their stones, and will spend three days setting them.

li.label: Let them, {B_nameDef} working beside them
li.outcome: The pilgrims are walking out to the {TALE} with their stones, and {B_nameDef} is going with them. It will take two days.

li.label: Leave the place as it is
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} blesses the gate on the way out anyway, as pilgrims do whether a door is opened to them or not, and the pilgrims walk on.

lines.li: [raise] A stone for every prayer said here before us.
[thanks] Bless this door, open or shut.
[day] Another course of stones, and the lamp tomorrow.
[bless] Blessed, and lit, and the colony's now.
[stop] A little for the road, and a little left here.

texts.li: [clash] {X_nameDef}, a palmer of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a shell on a cord. The fellowship heard that the followers of {TALE} and {DEAD} are quarrelling in the colony. {X_nameDef} would like everyone to eat at one table this evening, with {A_nameDef} speaking for one faith and {B_nameDef} for the other, and would bless the meal.

[split] {X_nameDef}, a palmer of {FACTION}, has stopped at the gate. {X_nameDef} has heard that the colony's followers of {TALE} are close to splitting, with some of them wavering. {X_nameDef} suggests a meal at one table this evening, where {A_nameDef} would speak for those who are sure and {B_nameDef} for those who are not, and would bless it.

[clash,age0|age1] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a palmer in a frayed cloak, has come to the gate. {X_nameDef} says Old Brannoc blessed every door, whether it opened to him or not, and suggests that the followers of {TALE} and {DEAD} share a table for one evening, with {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} speaking for each side.

[split,age0|age1] {X_nameDef}, a palmer of {FACTION}, has walked to the gate with a staff hung with shells. {X_nameDef} says a faith whose followers are wavering is helped more by a shared meal than by a sermon. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} could speak for {TALE} at supper this evening, and {X_nameDef} would bless the meal.

[clash,age2|age3] {X_nameDef}, a palmer of {FACTION} with a pack and a walking pole, has come to the gate. The fellowship heard that the followers of {TALE} and {DEAD} are quarrelling in the colony, and {X_nameDef} suggests they share a table this evening, with {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} speaking for each side and a blessing over the meal.

[split,age2|age3] {X_nameDef}, a palmer of {FACTION}, has walked to the gate with a pack and a walking pole. A faith whose followers are wavering is helped more by a shared meal than by a sermon, {X_nameDef} says: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} could speak for {TALE} at supper this evening, and {X_nameDef} would bless the meal.

[their:grateful] The fellowship remembers the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} came as soon as they heard about the trouble between its faiths. {X_nameDef} suggests a meal at one table this evening, with {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} speaking and a blessing over it.

li.label: Gather this evening; {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} speak
li.outcome: The colony will gather at one table this evening, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} to speak and {X_nameDef} to bless it.
li.riskOutcome: The colony gathered at one table and {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spoke, but it did not bring the two sides together.

lines.li: Bread for both sides of the table.
Let each speak, and the other listen.
One table, and one evening of it.
Bread for both sides of the table.
Let each speak, and the other listen.
One table, and one evening of it.

li.label: Let {X_objective} bless each side apart
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will walk about the colony and bless the believers of each side one by one, no speeches.

li.label: Thank {X_objective}, and send {X_objective} on
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} blesses the gate on the way out anyway, as pilgrims do whether a door is opened to them or not, and walks on.

lines.li: [table] One table, and room at it for everyone.
[walk] Each in turn, then, and no speeches.
[thanks] Bless this door, open or shut.
[settled] It held, and may it hold a season.
[split] It did not hold, and that is said plainly.
[bless] Steady now, whatever you believe.
[apart] Every one of them blessed, and the road is long.
